title: Slipstream: Semantic-Based Training Acceleration for Recommendation Models
problem: Recommendation model training suffers from redundant embedding updates; even after separating popular and non-popular embeddings, certain popular embeddings saturate early and undergo minimal subsequent variation.
motivation: Recommendation systems are resource-intensive to train; eliminating redundant gradient updates reduces CPU-GPU bandwidth and memory access, improving training throughput.
method: Slipstream framework identifies stale embeddings (those that have saturated and stopped changing) on-the-fly and skips their gradient updates. Monitors embedding variation during training and detects saturation. Combines with existing popular/non-popular classification for greater savings.
key_novelty: On-the-fly saturation detection for embeddings, skipping updates to non-varying embeddings while maintaining model accuracy.
contributions: Maintains accuracy while discarding redundant updates
Optimizes CPU-GPU bandwidth and memory access

metrics.speedup: 2x vs XDL, 2.4x vs DRLM, 1.2x vs FAE, 1.175x vs Hotline

limitations: Evaluation limited to specific recommendation models and datasets; generalization to other sparse embedding workloads unclear.
primary_theme: recommendation training via stale embedding skipping
